title: Ezekiel Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 1.

questions.question: Where was Ezekiel when he saw visions of God?
questions.correctAnswer: By the river of Chebar
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was among the captives by the river of Chebar when he saw visions of God, as stated in Ezekiel 1:1.

questions.question: In which year of King Jehoiachin's captivity did Ezekiel receive the word of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Fifth year
questions.explanation: The word of the LORD came to Ezekiel in the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's captivity, as indicated in Ezekiel 1:2.

questions.question: What relation to Buzi is Ezekiel described as?
questions.correctAnswer: Son
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is described as the son of Buzi in Ezekiel 1:3.

questions.question: What came out of the north as Ezekiel looked?
options: A whirlwind, a great cloud, and fire
questions.correctAnswer: A whirlwind, a great cloud, and fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel saw a whirlwind come out of the north, a great cloud, and fire infolding itself, as described in Ezekiel 1:4.

questions.question: How many living creatures did Ezekiel see?
questions.correctAnswer: Four
questions.explanation: Ezekiel saw four living creatures coming out of the midst of the fire, as stated in Ezekiel 1:5.

questions.question: How many faces did each living creature have?
questions.correctAnswer: Four
questions.explanation: Each living creature had four faces, as described in Ezekiel 1:6.

questions.question: What kind of feet did the living creatures have?
options: Straight feet like a calf's foot
questions.correctAnswer: Straight feet like a calf's foot
questions.explanation: Their feet were straight feet and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot, as stated in Ezekiel 1:7.

questions.question: Where were the hands of the living creatures located?
options: Under their wings on their four sides
questions.correctAnswer: Under their wings on their four sides
questions.explanation: The living creatures had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides, as described in Ezekiel 1:8.

questions.question: True or False: The wings of the living creatures were joined to one another.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:9 states that their wings were joined one to another.

questions.question: Which of the following faces did the living creatures NOT have?
questions.correctAnswer: Serpent
questions.explanation: The four faces were of a man, a lion, an ox, and an eagle; serpent is not mentioned, as stated in Ezekiel 1:10.

questions.question: True or False: The wings of the living creatures covered their bodies on both sides.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Each living creature had two wings stretched upward joined to another, and two wings covering their bodies on each side, as described in Ezekiel 1:11.

questions.question: What did the feet of the living creatures sparkle like?
questions.correctAnswer: Burnished brass
questions.explanation: Their feet sparkled like the colour of burnished brass, as stated in Ezekiel 1:7.

questions.question: How did the living creatures move according to Ezekiel 1?
questions.correctAnswer: Straight forward without turning
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:9 says the living creatures did not turn when they went but went straight forward.

questions.question: Which came first in Ezekiel's vision: the whirlwind or the living creatures?
questions.correctAnswer: Whirlwind
questions.explanation: The whirlwind came out of the north first, then out of the midst came the four living creatures, as indicated in Ezekiel 1:4-5.

questions.question: True or False: The hand of the LORD was upon Ezekiel when the word came to him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:3 states that the hand of the LORD was upon him when the word of the LORD came expressly to him.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How are the wings of the living creatures described in Ezekiel 1:11?
options: Two wings stretched upward, joined one to another, and two covered their bodies
All wings were folded tightly against their bodies
Only one wing each, stretched outward
Four wings each, all flapping constantly
questions.correctAnswer: Two wings stretched upward, joined one to another, and two covered their bodies
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:11 states that the wings were stretched upward, two of each creature's wings were joined one to another, and two covered their bodies, indicating a specific formation and movement.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 1:12, what determines the direction in which the living creatures move?
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit's direction
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:12 explains that the living creatures went straight forward wherever the spirit was to go, emphasizing the guidance by the spirit rather than external factors.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Ezekiel 1:13 to describe the appearance of the living creatures?
options: Burning coals of fire and lamps with lightning coming forth
Stars shining brightly in the night
Clouds moving swiftly in the sky
questions.correctAnswer: Burning coals of fire and lamps with lightning coming forth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:13 describes the living creatures as resembling burning coals of fire and lamps, with bright fire and lightning proceeding from them, symbolizing intense divine energy.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 1:14 describe the movement of the living creatures?
options: They ran and returned like a flash of lightning
They moved slowly like a creeping vine
They marched steadily like an army
questions.correctAnswer: They ran and returned like a flash of lightning
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:14 states that the living creatures ran and returned with the appearance of a flash of lightning, emphasizing their swift and powerful movement.

questions.question: What is unique about the wheels associated with the living creatures as described in Ezekiel 1:15?
options: Each wheel had four faces, just like the living creatures
The wheels were made of pure gold
questions.correctAnswer: Each wheel had four faces, just like the living creatures
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:15 highlights that each wheel beside the living creatures had four faces, mirroring the four faces of the creatures themselves, linking the two closely.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 1:16, how are the wheels described in appearance and construction?
options: Like a wheel in the middle of a wheel, with the color of beryl
Simple wooden wheels with iron rims
Wheels made of stone with no special features
questions.correctAnswer: Like a wheel in the middle of a wheel, with the color of beryl
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:16 describes the wheels as having the appearance and work like a wheel in the middle of a wheel, with a color resembling beryl, indicating complexity and brilliance.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 1:17 say about the movement and turning of the wheels?
options: They went upon their four sides and did not turn when they went
They could only move forward and backward
They spun continuously without moving forward
questions.correctAnswer: They went upon their four sides and did not turn when they went
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:17 states that the wheels moved on their four sides and did not turn as they moved, symbolizing direct and purposeful movement.

questions.question: How are the rings of the wheels described in Ezekiel 1:18?
options: Dreadful in height and full of eyes around them
Smooth and shiny without any markings
questions.correctAnswer: Dreadful in height and full of eyes around them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:18 describes the rings of the wheels as being so high that they were dreadful, and full of eyes all around, conveying awe and vigilance.

questions.question: What connection between the living creatures and the wheels does Ezekiel 1:19 illustrate?
options: When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved; when they were lifted, the wheels lifted
The wheels moved independently of the creatures
The creatures controlled the wheels by voice commands only
The wheels remained stationary while the creatures moved
questions.correctAnswer: When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved; when they were lifted, the wheels lifted
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:19 explains that the wheels followed the living creatures precisely, moving and lifting as the creatures did, showing unity in their movement.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 1:20, what causes the wheels to move and be lifted?
options: The spirit of the living creature within the wheels
The sound of the creatures' wings
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit of the living creature within the wheels
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:20 states that the wheels moved according to the spirit of the living creatures because the spirit was in the wheels, showing divine animation.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 1:12 teach us about faith and obedience in following God's guidance?
options: We should move straight forward in the direction the spirit leads without turning back
We should always question the spirit's direction before moving
We should only move when it is convenient for us
We should rely on our own understanding instead of the spirit
questions.correctAnswer: We should move straight forward in the direction the spirit leads without turning back
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:12 shows the living creatures moving straight forward wherever the spirit directed them, teaching believers to trust and obey God's guidance faithfully and without hesitation.

questions.question: Based on Ezekiel 1:19-20, what biblical truth applies when a believer feels spiritually lifted or moved by God's Spirit?
options: The believer's life is connected to the Spirit's movement and should respond accordingly
The believer should resist all changes as they are uncertain
The believer must rely solely on their own strength
The believer should ignore spiritual promptings
questions.correctAnswer: The believer's life is connected to the Spirit's movement and should respond accordingly
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:19-20 illustrate that the wheels moved because the spirit of the living creatures was in them, teaching that believers are meant to move and act in harmony with the Spirit's leading.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 1:13 describes the living creatures as having the appearance of lamps with fire and lightning going forth from them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:13 directly states that the living creatures' appearance was like burning coals of fire and lamps, with fire bright and lightning going forth, confirming the statement.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 1:17, the wheels turned in all directions as they moved.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:17 clearly states the wheels did not turn as they went; they moved straight upon their four sides, disproving the idea of turning in all directions.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 1:18 teaches that the rings of the wheels were full of eyes, symbolizing awareness and vigilance.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:18 describes the rings of the wheels as full of eyes all around, which can be understood as a symbol of constant awareness and vigilance in God's presence.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 1.

questions.question: What is the significance of the wheels being 'lifted up over against' the living creatures in Ezekiel's vision?
options: It symbolizes their independence from the living creatures
It shows that the spirit of the living creatures is in the wheels
It indicates that the wheels are separate beings
It represents the wheels being inactive
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that the spirit of the living creatures is in the wheels
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:21 explains that when the living creatures moved, the wheels moved alongside them because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels, indicating unity of movement and purpose.

questions.question: How is the 'firmament' described in Ezekiel 1:22, and what might this imagery suggest about its nature?
options: A fiery blaze stretched over the creatures
A terrible crystal stretched forth over their heads
A dark cloud overshadowing the creatures
A golden canopy shining above them
questions.correctAnswer: A terrible crystal stretched forth over their heads
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:22 describes the firmament as 'the colour of the terrible crystal,' suggesting a majestic, awe-inspiring, and possibly divine barrier or expanse above the living creatures.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 1:23, how were the wings positioned under the firmament in relation to each other and their bodies?
options: All wings were folded tightly against their bodies
The wings were spread outwards away from each other
Two wings of each creature covered their bodies, and two were straight toward each other
All wings were raised upwards and apart
questions.correctAnswer: Two wings of each creature covered their bodies, and two were straight toward each other
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:23 states that under the firmament, the wings were straight, one toward the other; each creature had two wings that covered their bodies on one side and two on the other, indicating a protective and symmetrical arrangement.

questions.question: What sound did Ezekiel hear from the wings of the living creatures when they moved, as per Ezekiel 1:24?
options: The sound of great waters and the voice of the Almighty
questions.correctAnswer: The sound of great waters and the voice of the Almighty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:24 describes the noise of their wings as like the noise of great waters, the voice of the Almighty, and the voice of speech, highlighting the overwhelming and divine nature of the vision.

questions.question: What happened when the living creatures stood and let down their wings in Ezekiel 1:25?
options: There was a voice from the firmament over their heads
questions.correctAnswer: There was a voice from the firmament over their heads
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:25 states that when the creatures stood and had let down their wings, a voice came from the firmament over their heads, indicating communication or divine presence associated with their movements.

questions.question: What was above the firmament over the living creatures’ heads, according to Ezekiel 1:26?
options: The likeness of a throne as the appearance of a sapphire stone
questions.correctAnswer: The likeness of a throne as the appearance of a sapphire stone
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:26 describes a throne above the firmament, appearing like sapphire, symbolizing divine authority and majesty above the living creatures.

questions.question: How did Ezekiel describe the figure on the throne in terms of color and appearance in Ezekiel 1:27?
options: Like pure gold with a crown of stars
Like amber with fire round about from the loins upward and downward
Like a cloud with lightning flashing
questions.correctAnswer: Like amber with fire round about from the loins upward and downward
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:27 states that the figure on the throne appeared like the colour of amber with fire and brightness round about, symbolizing holiness, power, and divine glory.

questions.question: What natural phenomenon does Ezekiel compare to the brightness around the figure on the throne in Ezekiel 1:28?
options: The rainbow in the cloud on a rainy day
questions.correctAnswer: The rainbow in the cloud on a rainy day
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:28 compares the brightness around the figure to a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day, symbolizing God's covenantal glory and mercy.

questions.question: True or False: The spirit of the living creatures was also present in the wheels that accompanied them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:21 and 1:20 explain that the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels, causing them to move together in unison.

questions.question: True or False: The wings of the living creatures were always folded and never stretched upwards.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:11 states that their wings were stretched upward, with two wings joined together and two covering their bodies, indicating they were not always folded.

questions.question: Which other biblical text shares a similar vision of heavenly creatures with multiple faces and wheels, suggesting a thematic connection with Ezekiel 1?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 4
questions.explanation: Revelation 4 describes four living creatures around the throne with multiple faces and wings, echoing Ezekiel's vision in Ezekiel 1:5-28, emphasizing divine throne-room imagery.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 1:18, what unique feature is described about the rings of the wheels, and what might this symbolize?
options: The rings were golden and smooth, symbolizing peace
The rings were full of eyes, symbolizing divine awareness
The rings were fiery, symbolizing destruction
The rings were covered with jewels, symbolizing wealth
questions.correctAnswer: The rings were full of eyes, symbolizing divine awareness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:18 describes the rings as 'full of eyes round about them,' which symbolizes all-seeing divine knowledge and vigilance.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is used in Ezekiel 1 to describe the 'living creatures,' and what is its significance in ancient Near Eastern iconography?
options: Chayot, indicating divine angelic beings with complex symbolism
questions.correctAnswer: Chayot, indicating divine angelic beings with complex symbolism
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Chayot' (חַיּוֹת) used in Ezekiel 1:5 refers to 'living creatures,' representing angelic beings with multifaceted faces and wings, common in ancient Near Eastern visions of divine presence.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 1 to structure the vision of the creatures and wheels, emphasizing their complexity and unity?
options: Chiasm, highlighting parallelism between creatures and wheels
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm, highlighting parallelism between creatures and wheels
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1 employs chiasm by paralleling the living creatures and the wheels (e.g., verses 15-21), reflecting their interdependence and unity in the vision structure.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel's vision in chapter 1 foreshadow New Testament descriptions of Christ’s divine glory?
options: Through the description of the amber and fire imagery around the figure on the throne
By depicting Christ as a shepherd
By focusing on the Messiah's genealogy
questions.correctAnswer: Through the description of the amber and fire imagery around the figure on the throne
questions.explanation: The amber and fire imagery in Ezekiel 1:27 resembles the glorified Christ described in Revelation 1:14-15, suggesting Ezekiel's vision prefigures New Testament Christology.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the vision of the four living creatures with four faces and four wings in Ezekiel 1:5-6 and their joined wings in Ezekiel 1:11 illustrate about God's nature?
options: God's judgment limited to one direction
God's absence from the physical world
questions.correctAnswer: God's multifaceted and omnipresent nature
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:5-6 describes the living creatures having four faces and four wings, and Ezekiel 1:11 explains their wings were joined, symbolizing unity and omnipresence. This denotes God's multifaceted attributes and His presence everywhere simultaneously.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 1:4, what does the whirlwind, great cloud, and fire infolding itself symbolize about the divine presence?
questions.correctAnswer: God's dynamic power and holiness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:4 depicts a whirlwind, cloud, and fire with brightness around it, representing the powerful and holy presence of God, as fire often symbolizes God's holiness (Exodus 3:2).

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the wheels 'full of eyes round about' in Ezekiel 1:18?
options: God's limitation to one earthly region
questions.correctAnswer: God's omniscience and all-seeing nature
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:18 describes wheels full of eyes, symbolizing God's omniscience — His perfect knowledge and ability to see all things, consistent with Psalm 33:13-15.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 1:26-27's description of the throne and the figure above it contribute to Christological understanding?
options: It foreshadows the pre-incarnate glory of Christ seated in divine authority
It depicts a human king unrelated to divine beings
It refers only to an angelic being
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the pre-incarnate glory of Christ seated in divine authority
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:26-27 presents a figure like a man on a throne with fire and brightness, symbolizing divine glory and authority, which Christian theology understands as a pre-incarnate appearance of Christ (cf. John 1:1-14).

questions.question: What does the movement of the living creatures and wheels 'whithersoever the spirit was to go' in Ezekiel 1:12 and 1:20 teach about the Spirit of God?
options: The Spirit directs divine action and is sovereign over all movement
The Spirit is passive and limited to specific places
The Spirit is dependent on human will
The Spirit is unrelated to God's presence
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit directs divine action and is sovereign over all movement
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:12 and 1:20 show the living creatures and wheels moving according to the Spirit's direction, highlighting the Spirit's sovereignty and active role in God's operation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Ezekiel's vision in chapter 1 is merely a product of hallucination with no divine origin. What does Ezekiel 1:3 and 1:28 teach about the nature of this vision?
options: The vision is a direct, divinely-initiated revelation accompanied by the glory of the LORD
The vision is a personal dream with no theological significance
The vision is a common mythological story
The vision is symbolic folklore with no real encounter
questions.correctAnswer: The vision is a direct, divinely-initiated revelation accompanied by the glory of the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:3 states the word of the LORD came expressly to Ezekiel, and 1:28 describes the glory of the LORD causing Ezekiel to fall on his face, affirming the vision's divine origin and authority.

questions.question: What attribute of God is primarily highlighted by the noise of the wings described as 'like the noise of great waters' and 'the voice of the Almighty' in Ezekiel 1:24?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence and majestic sovereignty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:24 uses imagery of overwhelming noise likened to great waters and the voice of the Almighty, portraying God's powerful and sovereign presence over all creation (cf. Psalm 93:3-4).

questions.question: How does the description of the living creatures’ feet 'like the sole of a calf’s foot' and 'sparkled like burnished brass' in Ezekiel 1:7 symbolize a theological truth?
options: The purity and stability of God's heavenly beings
The earthly origin of the vision
The unclean nature of the creatures
questions.correctAnswer: The purity and stability of God's heavenly beings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:7 compares the feet to a calf's sole and burnished brass, symbolizing strength, purity, and steadfastness, reflecting the holy nature of the beings serving God.

questions.question: What narrative role does Ezekiel 1:1-2 establish in the context of Israel’s exile and divine revelation?
options: It situates the vision during captivity, indicating God’s active presence even in exile
It shows God has abandoned Israel
It illustrates a historical event unrelated to divine revelation
It focuses solely on political power
questions.correctAnswer: It situates the vision during captivity, indicating God’s active presence even in exile
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:1-2 place the vision during captivity by the river Chebar, emphasizing that God remains present and sovereign even amid Israel’s exile, a key theme in redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight is taught by Ezekiel 1:15-16 and Ezekiel 1:19-21 regarding God’s providence?
options: God’s providence is comprehensive, sustaining all creation with coordinated, purposeful movement
God is unaware of earthly affairs
God’s providence is random and uncoordinated
God is limited to certain geographic regions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence is comprehensive, sustaining all creation with coordinated, purposeful movement
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:15-16 describe the wheels ‘like a wheel in the middle of a wheel,’ and 1:19-21 show wheels moving in unison with the living creatures, illustrating God’s meticulous providential control over all creation’s actions.

questions.question: What does the firmament 'as the colour of terrible crystal' over the heads of the living creatures in Ezekiel 1:22 signify about God's holiness and transcendence?
options: God’s holiness is pure, awe-inspiring, and separates the divine from the earthly realm
God has no distinct presence above creation
God’s holiness is common and unremarkable
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness is pure, awe-inspiring, and separates the divine from the earthly realm
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:22’s description of the firmament as crystal highlights the purity and awe of God's holiness, emphasizing divine transcendence above creation (cf. Isaiah 6:1-4).

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth about divine communication is evidenced by Ezekiel 1:3, where 'the word of the LORD came expressly unto Ezekiel'?
options: God communicates clearly and authoritatively through chosen prophets
God is silent and inaccessible to humans
Prophetic messages are vague and uncertain
Divine communication is always indirect and hidden
questions.correctAnswer: God communicates clearly and authoritatively through chosen prophets
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:3 states the word of the LORD came expressly to Ezekiel, affirming that God reveals His will clearly through prophets, a key doctrine of divine revelation (cf. 2 Timothy 3:16).

questions.question: How do the multiple faces of the living creatures—man, lion, ox, and eagle—as described in Ezekiel 1:10, contribute to an understanding of God's creation and authority?
options: They symbolize God's sovereign rule over all aspects of creation—humanity, wild animals, domesticated animals, and birds
They indicate confusion and disorder in creation
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolize God's sovereign rule over all aspects of creation—humanity, wild animals, domesticated animals, and birds
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:10 assigns four faces to the creatures, representing different realms of creation, illustrating God's comprehensive authority and care over all life.

questions.question: What does the description of the fire and brightness around the figure on the throne in Ezekiel 1:27-28 teach about God's glory?
options: God's glory is radiant, consuming, and awe-inspiring
God's glory is dim and hidden
God's glory is separate from divine presence
questions.correctAnswer: God's glory is radiant, consuming, and awe-inspiring
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:27-28 describes fire and brightness surrounding the figure, likened to a rainbow’s brightness, signifying God's majestic, radiant, and consuming glory, causing Ezekiel to fall on his face.

questions.question: What combined teaching about the unity of divine beings and the divine order is conveyed by Ezekiel 1:8 and Ezekiel 1:23 regarding the living creatures' wings and bodies?
options: The creatures' wings cover their bodies and are arranged harmoniously, symbolizing divine unity and order
The creatures are disorganized and chaotic
The creatures are independent with conflicting purposes
questions.correctAnswer: The creatures' wings cover their bodies and are arranged harmoniously, symbolizing divine unity and order
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 1:8 describes hands under wings and 1:23 depicts wings covering bodies, illustrating the harmonious unity and order among divine beings reflecting God’s perfect governance.
